Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 66, verse 1–5:

(p-302) Surat at-Tahrim

It is Madani in its entirety, by the consensus of the scholars.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Why do you prohibit what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ There are two reports concerning the occasion of its revelation.

The first: "Hafsa went to her father to converse with him, and the Prophet ﷺ sent for his slave-girl, and she remained with him in Hafsa's house, on the day when he would come to 'Aisha. (p-303) Hafsa returned, found her in her house, and began waiting for her to come out, and she was overcome with intense jealousy. When Hafsa entered, she said: 'I have seen who was with you. By Allah, you have hurt me.' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'By Allah, I will satisfy you, and I am going to tell you a secret, so keep it.' She said: 'And what is it?' He said: 'I call you to witness that this slave-girl of mine is forbidden to me, for your pleasure.' 'Aisha and Hafsa were supporting each other against the wives of the Prophet ﷺ. Hafsa went to 'Aisha and said to her: 'Rejoice, for the Prophet ﷺ has forbidden his concubine to himself.' Then this verse was revealed." Narrated by al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas. It has also been narrated from 'Umar a meaning similar to this, and in it he said: "Hafsa said: 'How can you forbid her to yourself when she is your slave-girl?!' So he swore to her that he would not approach her, and he said to her: 'Do not mention it to anyone.' She mentioned it to 'Aisha, so he took an oath that he would not enter upon his wives for a month, and then this verse was revealed." Al-Dahhak said: "He said to her: 'Do not mention to 'Aisha what you have seen,' but she mentioned it, and 'Aisha became angry and kept after the Prophet of Allah until he swore that he would not approach her, and then this verse was revealed." To this view went Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, 'Ata', al-Sha'bi, Masruq, Muqatil, and most of the scholars.

The second: what 'Urwa narrated from 'Aisha, who said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ loved sweets and honey, and when he finished the 'Asr prayer he would enter upon his wives. He entered upon Hafsa bint 'Umar and stayed with her longer than usual, so I asked about that, and it was said: 'A woman from her people had given her a jar of honey as a gift, and she gave the Messenger of Allah ﷺ a drink of it.' I said: 'By Allah, we will certainly devise a plan against him.' I said to Sawda: 'When he comes close to you as he enters upon you, say to him: "O Messenger of Allah, have you eaten maghafir?" For he will say to you: "Hafsa gave me a drink of honey." So say: "Its bees have grazed on 'urfut."' I will say that too, and you, O Safiyya, say the same.' When he came round to Hafsa, she said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, shall I give you a drink of it?' He said: 'I have no need for it.' She said: 'Sawda says: Glory be to Allah! By Allah, we have deprived him of it.' I said to her: 'Be quiet.'" Related by al-Bukhari and Muslim in the two Sahihs. In the narration of Ibn Abi Mulayka from Ibn 'Abbas: (p-305) the one with whom he drank the honey was Sawda; 'Aisha said to him: "I smell a odour from you," then he entered upon Hafsa, and she said: "I smell an odour from you." He said: "I think it is from a drink I took at Sawda's. By Allah, I will not drink it," and then this verse was revealed. In the hadith of 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr from 'Aisha, the one with whom he drank the honey was Zaynab bint Jahsh, and Hafsa and 'Aisha agreed together to say that statement to him. Abu 'Ubayd said: al-maghafir is a substance similar to gum, which has sweetness in it; and people went out "yatamaghfarun" meaning, when they went out they gathered it. It is also said: al-maghathir with the thaa', like judath and judaf. al-Zajjaj said: al-maghafir is gum whose smell has changed. So there are two views concerning what is meant by "that which Allah has made lawful for him." (p-306) The first: it is his slave-girl. The second: honey.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿seeking the pleasure of your wives﴾, i.e., seeking their contentment by prohibiting that. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, Allah has forgiven you the prohibition. ﴿Allah has already ordained for you﴾. Muqatil said: Allah has already explained for you ﴿the dissolution of your oaths﴾, i.e., the expiation of your oaths, and that explanation is in [al-Ma'idah: 89]. The exegetes said: the original form of "tahillah" is tahlilah, on the pattern of taf'ilah, and it was assimilated; the meaning is: Allah has already explained for you the dissolution of your oaths through expiation, so Allah commanded him to expiate his oath, and he freed a slave.

(p-307) They differed over whether he prohibited Maria to himself by an oath or not, on two views.

The first: he prohibited her without mentioning an oath, so the prohibition required the expiation of an oath. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: he swore an oath by which he prohibited her. This was said by al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi, and Qatadah. ﴿And Allah is your Protector﴾, i.e., your Guardian and your Helper.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement﴾, meaning Hafsa, without any disagreement that we know of.

Regarding this secret there are three views.

The first: he said to her: "I am going to tell you a secret, so keep it: this slave-girl of mine is forbidden to me." Narrated by al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas, and 'Ata', al-Sha'bi, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Zayd ibn Aslam and his son, and al-Suddi also said so.

(p-308) The second: he said to her: "Your father and the father of 'Aisha will be rulers of the people after me, so beware of telling anyone." Narrated by Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas.

The third: he confided to her that Abu Bakr would be my successor after me. This was said by Maymun ibn Mihran.

(p-309) His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So when she informed of it﴾, i.e., she told 'Aisha about it, "and Allah made him aware of it", i.e., Allah informed His Prophet of Hafsa's statement to 'Aisha, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became greatly angry, because he had asked Hafsa to keep it secret. Then he summoned her and told her part of what she had said, and that is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He made known part of it and overlooked part﴾. Concerning what he made known to her, there are two views.

The first: he told her what 'Aisha had told her about Abu Bakr and 'Umar, and he kept silent about what she had told 'Aisha concerning the prohibition of Maria, because he did not mind what she had disclosed of that. Narrated by Abu Salih from Ibn 'Abbas.

The second: what he made known was the prohibition of Maria, and what he overlooked was the mention of the caliphate, lest it spread. This was said by al-Dahhak, and this is the preference of al-Zajjaj. He said: the meaning of "He made known part of it" is that he made known to Hafsa part of it. Al-Kisa'i read "'arafa" with light pronunciation. al-Zajjaj said: according to this reading, he made known all that he had confided, except that the meaning is applied to part of it, like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whatever good you do, Allah knows it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 179], i.e., He knows it and will recompense for it; and likewise: ﴿Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 7], i.e., will see its recompense. It was said: the Prophet ﷺ divorced Hafsa once, and that was her recompense from him, so Allah commanded him to take her back. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: he did not divorce her, but he intended to divorce her, and Jibril said to him: "Do not divorce her, for she is fasting often and standing in prayer often." al-Hasan said: no generous person ever pressed for every detail, then he recited ﴿He made known part of it and overlooked part﴾. Ibn Mas'ud, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and Ibn al-Sumayfa' read "'urrafa" with a raised 'ayn, doubled ra', and with an alif, and "ba'dihi" with a kasra.

(p-310) His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So when he informed her of it﴾, i.e., he told Hafsa that she had disclosed the secret, ﴿she said: "Who told you this?"﴾, i.e., who informed you that I had disclosed your secret? ﴿He said: "I was informed by the All-Knowing, the All-Aware."﴾ Then He addressed 'Aisha and Hafsa, saying: ﴿If you two repent to Allah﴾, i.e., from cooperating against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by causing him harm, ﴿then your hearts have indeed inclined﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: they deviated and sinned. al-Zajjaj said: they swerved and deviated from the truth. Mujahid said: we used to regard His saying, the Exalted: ﴿then your hearts have indeed inclined﴾ as something minor, until we found it in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "then your hearts have indeed deviated." He made the two hearts plural because any two or more is a plurality. We have already pointed out this in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿But if he has brothers﴾ [an-Nisa': 11] and His saying: ﴿when they climbed over the wall of the prayer niche﴾ [Sad: 21]. The exegetes said: this is because the two of them loved what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked, namely avoiding his slave-girl. ﴿And if you cooperate against him﴾. Ibn Mas'ud, Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, Mujahid, and al-A'mash read "tazahara" with a light zay, i.e., cooperated against the Prophet ﷺ by causing him harm. ﴿Then indeed Allah is his Protector﴾, i.e., his Guardian in support and aid. ﴿And Gabriel﴾ is his Guardian, ﴿and the righteous among the believers﴾. Concerning what is meant by "the righteous among the believers" there are six views.

The first: they are Abu Bakr and 'Umar. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud, 'Ikrimah, and al-Dahhak.

The second: Abu Bakr, narrated by Makhul from Abu Umamah.

The third: 'Umar, said by Ibn Jubayr and Mujahid.

The fourth: the best of the believers, said by al-Rabi' ibn Anas.

(p-311) The fifth: they are the prophets, said by Qatadah, al-'Ala' ibn Ziyad al-'Adawi, and Sufyan.

The sixth: it is 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, related by al-Mawardi. al-Farra' said: ﴿and the righteous among the believers﴾ is singular in the usage of all, as you say: "None comes to me except the leader of the war," so whoever is a leader for war has been commanded to come; and similar to this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿As for the thief, male and female﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 38], and His saying: ﴿And those two of you who commit it﴾ [an-Nisa': 16], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind was created anxious﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 19], and in many places in the Qur'an, the singular expresses the meaning of the plural.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the angels thereafter are supporters﴾, i.e., a supporting group. This is one of those expressions whose wording is singular but whose meaning is plural; similar to it is ﴿He brings you forth as a child﴾ [Ghafir: 67], which we have explained there.

The occasion of its revelation was what Anas narrated from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: "News reached me of some of what the wives of the Messenger of Allah had caused him harm with, so I went to them and began questioning them one by one, and I said: 'By Allah, you will desist, or Allah will replace him with wives better than you,' and then this verse was revealed." The meaning: it is binding from Allah that ﴿if he divorced you﴾, His Messenger, ﴿he would give him in exchange wives better than you, submitting﴾, i.e., humbly obedient to Allah in worship, ﴿believing﴾, affirming the Oneness of Allah, ﴿devoutly obedient﴾, i.e., obedient, ﴿repentant﴾. Concerning "sa'ihat" there are two views. (p-312)

The first: fasting, said by Ibn 'Abbas and the majority. We have explained this meaning at His saying, the Exalted: ﴿the wanderers﴾ [at-Tawbah: 112].

The second: emigrating, said by Zayd ibn Aslam and his son. "Ath-thayyibat" is the plural of thayyib, the woman who has been married and then returned to her parents' house and became as she was before, no longer married. "Al-abkar" are the virgins.

The second: he swore an oath by which he prohibited her. This was said by al-Hasan, al-Sha'bi, and Qatadah. ﴿And Allah is your Protector﴾, i.e., your Guardian and your Helper.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement﴾, meaning Hafsa, without any disagreement that we know of.

Regarding this secret there are three views.

The first: he said to her: "I am going to tell you a secret, so keep it: this slave-girl of mine is forbidden to me." Narrated by al-Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas, and 'Ata', al-Sha'bi, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, Zayd ibn Aslam and his son, and al-Suddi also said so.

Al-Kisa'i read "'arafa" with light pronunciation. al-Zajjaj said: according to this reading, he made known all that he had confided, except that the meaning is applied to part of it, like His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whatever good you do, Allah knows it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 179], i.e., He knows it and will recompense for it; and likewise: ﴿Whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it﴾ [al-Zalzalah: 7], i.e., will see its recompense. It was said: the Prophet ﷺ divorced Hafsa once, and that was her recompense from him, so Allah commanded him to take her back. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: he did not divorce her, but he intended to divorce her, and Jibril said to him: "Do not divorce her, for she is fasting often and standing in prayer often." al-Hasan said: no generous person ever pressed for every detail, then he recited ﴿He made known part of it and overlooked part﴾. Ibn Mas'ud, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and Ibn al-Sumayfa' read "'urrafa" with a raised 'ayn, doubled ra', and with an alif, and "ba'dihi" with a kasra.

(p-310) His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So when he informed her of it﴾, i.e., he told Hafsa that she had disclosed the secret, ﴿she said: "Who told you this?"﴾, i.e., who informed you that I had disclosed your secret? ﴿He said: "I was informed by the All-Knowing, the All-Aware."﴾ Then He addressed 'Aisha and Hafsa, saying: ﴿If you two repent to Allah﴾, i.e., from cooperating against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ by causing him harm, ﴿then your hearts have indeed inclined﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: they deviated and sinned. al-Zajjaj said: they swerved and deviated from the truth. Mujahid said: we used to regard His saying, the Exalted: ﴿then your hearts have indeed inclined﴾ as something minor, until we found it in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "then your hearts have indeed deviated." He made the two hearts plural because any two or more is a plurality. We have already pointed out this in His saying, the Exalted: ﴿But if he has brothers﴾ [an-Nisa': 11] and His saying: ﴿when they climbed over the wall of the prayer niche﴾ [Sad: 21]. The exegetes said: this is because the two of them loved what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ disliked, namely avoiding his slave-girl. ﴿And if you cooperate against him﴾. Ibn Mas'ud, Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, Mujahid, and al-A'mash read "tazahara" with a light zay, i.e., cooperated against the Prophet ﷺ by causing him harm. ﴿Then indeed Allah is his Protector﴾, i.e., his Guardian in support and aid. ﴿And Gabriel﴾ is his Guardian, ﴿and the righteous among the believers﴾. Concerning what is meant by "the righteous among the believers" there are six views.

The first: they are Abu Bakr and 'Umar. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud, 'Ikrimah, and al-Dahhak.

The second: Abu Bakr, narrated by Makhul from Abu Umamah.

The third: 'Umar, said by Ibn Jubayr and Mujahid.

The fourth: the best of the believers, said by al-Rabi' ibn Anas.

(p-311) The fifth: they are the prophets, said by Qatadah, al-'Ala' ibn Ziyad al-'Adawi, and Sufyan.

The sixth: it is 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, related by al-Mawardi. al-Farra' said: ﴿and the righteous among the believers﴾ is singular in the usage of all, as you say: "None comes to me except the leader of the war," so whoever is a leader for war has been commanded to come; and similar to this is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿As for the thief, male and female﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 38], and His saying: ﴿And those two of you who commit it﴾ [an-Nisa': 16], and His saying: ﴿Indeed, mankind was created anxious﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 19], and in many places in the Qur'an, the singular expresses the meaning of the plural.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And the angels thereafter are supporters﴾, i.e., a supporting group. This is one of those expressions whose wording is singular but whose meaning is plural; similar to it is ﴿He brings you forth as a child﴾ [Ghafir: 67], which we have explained there.

Then He warned his wives, saying: ﴿Perhaps his Lord, if he divorced you, would give him in exchange wives better than you﴾. The occasion of its revelation was what Anas narrated from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, who said: "News reached me of some of what the wives of the Messenger of Allah had caused him harm with, so I went to them and began questioning them one by one, and I said: 'By Allah, you will desist, or Allah will replace him with wives better than you,' and then this verse was revealed." The meaning: it is binding from Allah that ﴿if he divorced you﴾, His Messenger, ﴿he would give him in exchange wives better than you, submitting﴾, i.e., humbly obedient to Allah in worship, ﴿believing﴾, affirming the Oneness of Allah, ﴿devoutly obedient﴾, i.e., obedient, ﴿repentant﴾. Concerning "sa'ihat" there are two views. (p-312)

The first: fasting, said by Ibn 'Abbas and the majority. We have explained this meaning at His saying, the Exalted: ﴿the wanderers﴾ [at-Tawbah: 112].

The second: emigrating, said by Zayd ibn Aslam and his son. "Ath-thayyibat" is the plural of thayyib, the woman who has been married and then returned to her parents' house and became as she was before, no longer married. "Al-abkar" are the virgins.

**Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 66, verses 6–8:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Guard yourselves and your families against a Fire﴾. The guarding of the self is by carrying out the commands and avoiding the prohibitions. The guarding of the family is by ordering them to obey and forbidding them from disobedience. ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "Teach them and discipline them." ﴿Its fuel is people and stones﴾, which we have mentioned in [al-Baqarah: 24]. ﴿Over it are angels, stern, severe﴾ against the people of the Fire, ﴿severe﴾ toward them.

It has been said: "Stern of hearts, severe of bodies." Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "The guardians of the Fire are nineteen. The distance between the shoulders of one of them is a year's journey. His strength is such that he strikes with a mace, and by that one blow he drives seventy thousand [people] away, and they fall into the bottom of Hell." ﴿They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them﴾, meaning they do not oppose Him in what He orders. ﴿And they do what they are commanded﴾. Concerning this there are two views.

The first: they do not exceed what they are commanded. The second: they carry it out at its appointed time; they neither delay it nor advance it. It will be said to the people of the Fire: ﴿"O you who have disbelieved, do not make excuses today."﴾

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Turn to Allah in sincere repentance﴾. Abū Bakr, from ʿĀṣim, and Kharijah, from Nāfiʿ, read "nuṣūḥan" (نُصُوحًا) with a ḍammah on the nūn. The rest read it with a fatḥah. al-Zajjāj said: "Whoever reads it with a fatḥah, it is in the description of repentance, and its meaning is: a repentance that reaches the utmost in sincerity. The form fa'ūl (فَعُولٌ) is among the forms of the active participle used for intensification in description. One says: a man who is ṣabūr (صَبُورٌ, very patient) and shakūr (شَكُورٌ, very grateful)." As for whoever reads it with a ḍammah, its meaning is: they give sincere advice in it, sincere advice. It is said: "She gave him sincere advice (naṣaḥat lahu nuṣḥan), and naṣāḥah, and nuṣūḥan." Others said: "Whoever reads it with a ḍammah intends: a repentance of sincere advice to your own selves."

ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: "Sincere repentance is that the servant repents from the sin while he tells himself that he will not return to it." al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī was asked about sincere repentance and said: "Regret in the heart, seeking forgiveness with the tongue, abandoning [the sin] with the limbs, and resolving never to return." Ibn Masʿūd said: "Sincere repentance erases every bad deed," and then he recited this verse.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet﴾. We have already explained the meaning of "disgrace" (khizy, خِزْي) in [Āl ʿImrān: 192], and we have explained the meaning of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Their light running before them and on their right﴾ in [al-Ḥadīd: 12]. ﴿They say: "Our Lord, complete for us our light"﴾. This is when the believers see the light of the hypocrites being extinguished; they ask Allah, exalted is He, to complete for them [their light] and to bring them with it to Paradise. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "There is no one among the Muslims except that he is given a light on the Day of Resurrection. As for the hypocrite, his light is extinguished, and the believer is fearful of what he sees of the extinguishing of the hypocrite's light, so they say: ﴿"Our Lord, complete for us our light."﴾"

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 66, verse 9–12:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾. It has already been explained in [Surah al-Tawbah: 73].

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah﴾. The exegetes, among them Muqatil, said: this example contains a warning to ʿAʾishah and Hafsah that if they disobey their Lord, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) will not avail them anything. Muqatil said: the name of Noah's wife was "Wali'ah" (wālihah) and the name of Lot's wife was "Wali'ah" (wāli'ah).

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They were under two of Our righteous servants﴾, meaning Noah and Lot, peace be upon them, ﴿but they betrayed them﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: the wife of a prophet never committed adultery; their betrayal was only in religion. Noah's wife would tell the people that he was mad, and Lot's wife would point out the guests; when a guest arrived at night to Lot, she would light the fire, and when one arrived by day she would make smoke so that his people would know a guest had come to him. Al-Suddi said: their betrayal was their disbelief.

Al-Dahhak said: their betrayal was their tale-bearing (namimah). Ibn al-Sa'ib said: their betrayal was their hypocrisy.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿But they did not avail them against Allah in anything﴾, meaning they did not repel from them any of the punishment of Allah. This verse cuts off the hope of one who commits sin and expects that the righteousness of another will benefit him.

Then He informed that the disobedience of others does not harm the obedient, by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah presents an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh﴾, who was Asiyah daughter of Muzahim, may Allah be pleased with her. Yahya ibn Salam said: Allah struck the first example to warn ʿAʾishah and Hafsah, may Allah be pleased with them, and then struck this example for them to encourage them to hold fast to obedience. Asiyah had believed in Moses.

Abu Hurayrah said: Pharaoh drove stakes into her hands and feet, and whenever they dispersed from her, the angels would shade her. She said: ﴿My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise﴾, so Allah revealed to her her house in Paradise until she saw it before her death. ﴿And save me from Pharaoh and his deeds﴾. Regarding this there are two views:

One: that his deeds meant his intercourse. The second: that it meant his religion, related from Ibn ʿAbbas. ﴿And save me from the wrongdoing people﴾, meaning the people of the polytheists' religion.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Mary daughter of ʿImran, who guarded her chastity﴾. We have mentioned two views concerning this in Surah al-Anbiya' [92]. Whoever says it means the opening of her garment says that the pronoun in His saying ﴿so We blew into it﴾ refers to it, because Gabriel pulled the collar of her shirt and it entered into it. Whoever says it means the place of birth of the child says the pronoun is a reference to something unmentioned, because He only blew into her shirt, not into her private part.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And she affirmed the words of her Lord﴾. Concerning this there are two views:

One: that they are the words of Gabriel, ﴿I am only a messenger of your Lord﴾ [Maryam: 19].

The second: that the words are those contained in the revealed books of Allah. Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Abu Majlaz, and ʿAsim al-Jahdari read "bi-kalimati Rabbihā" in the singular. Ibn Kathir, Ibn ʿAmir, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr on the authority of ʿAsim read "wa-kitabihi" in the singular. Abu ʿAmr and Hafs on the authority of ʿAsim, and Kharijah on the authority of Nafi' read "wa-kutubihi" in the plural, meaning those sent down upon the prophets. Whoever reads "wa-kitabihi" takes it as a collective noun, as we explained at the end of [al-Baqarah: 285], and we explained there the qunut in detail [al-Baqarah: 116].

The meaning of the verse: she was among the obedient (al-qanitin), and for this reason He did not say "al-qanitat" (feminine).

Commentary of Ibn al-Jawzi (Zad al-Masir) on surah 66, verse 9–12:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾. It has already been explained in [Surah al-Tawbah: 73].

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Allah presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah﴾. The exegetes, among them Muqatil, said: this example contains a warning to ʿAʾishah and Hafsah that if they disobey their Lord, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) will not avail them anything. Muqatil said: the name of Noah's wife was "Wali'ah" (wālihah) and the name of Lot's wife was "Wali'ah" (wāli'ah).

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They were under two of Our righteous servants﴾, meaning Noah and Lot, peace be upon them, ﴿but they betrayed them﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: the wife of a prophet never committed adultery; their betrayal was only in religion. Noah's wife would tell the people that he was mad, and Lot's wife would point out the guests; when a guest arrived at night to Lot, she would light the fire, and when one arrived by day she would make smoke so that his people would know a guest had come to him. Al-Suddi said: their betrayal was their disbelief.

Al-Dahhak said: their betrayal was their tale-bearing (namimah). Ibn al-Sa'ib said: their betrayal was their hypocrisy.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿But they did not avail them against Allah in anything﴾, meaning they did not repel from them any of the punishment of Allah. This verse cuts off the hope of one who commits sin and expects that the righteousness of another will benefit him.

Then He informed that the disobedience of others does not harm the obedient, by His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah presents an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh﴾, who was Asiyah daughter of Muzahim, may Allah be pleased with her. Yahya ibn Salam said: Allah struck the first example to warn ʿAʾishah and Hafsah, may Allah be pleased with them, and then struck this example for them to encourage them to hold fast to obedience. Asiyah had believed in Moses.

Abu Hurayrah said: Pharaoh drove stakes into her hands and feet, and whenever they dispersed from her, the angels would shade her. She said: ﴿My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise﴾, so Allah revealed to her her house in Paradise until she saw it before her death. ﴿And save me from Pharaoh and his deeds﴾. Regarding this there are two views:

One: that his deeds meant his intercourse. The second: that it meant his religion, related from Ibn ʿAbbas. ﴿And save me from the wrongdoing people﴾, meaning the people of the polytheists' religion.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Mary daughter of ʿImran, who guarded her chastity﴾. We have mentioned two views concerning this in Surah al-Anbiya' [92]. Whoever says it means the opening of her garment says that the pronoun in His saying ﴿so We blew into it﴾ refers to it, because Gabriel pulled the collar of her shirt and it entered into it. Whoever says it means the place of birth of the child says the pronoun is a reference to something unmentioned, because He only blew into her shirt, not into her private part.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And she affirmed the words of her Lord﴾. Concerning this there are two views:

One: that they are the words of Gabriel, ﴿I am only a messenger of your Lord﴾ [Maryam: 19].

The second: that the words are those contained in the revealed books of Allah. Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Abu Majlaz, and ʿAsim al-Jahdari read "bi-kalimati Rabbihā" in the singular. Ibn Kathir, Ibn ʿAmir, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr on the authority of ʿAsim read "wa-kitabihi" in the singular. Abu ʿAmr and Hafs on the authority of ʿAsim, and Kharijah on the authority of Nafi' read "wa-kutubihi" in the plural, meaning those sent down upon the prophets. Whoever reads "wa-kitabihi" takes it as a collective noun, as we explained at the end of [al-Baqarah: 285], and we explained there the qunut in detail [al-Baqarah: 116].

The meaning of the verse: she was among the obedient (al-qanitin), and for this reason He did not say "al-qanitat" (feminine).
